principalClaims.title: Denominator obstruction to a new sign row
principalClaims.statementTeX:
\label{trd:denom}
Let $n=4m$ with $m>1$ odd, and let $p$ be the least prime factor of $m$.
Suppose a sign vector $x$ lies in the real span of $r<n$ rows
$h_1,\ldots,h_r$ of an order-$n$ Hadamard matrix, but is not any
$\pm h_i$. Then
\begin{equation}\label{trd:bound}
 p\le\frac{r^{r/2}}{2^{r-1}}.
\end{equation}
More precisely, the least common denominator of the expansion
coefficients of $x$ divides $m$ and divides the normalized determinant
$\det S/2^{r-1}$ of every invertible $r\times r$ sign-column anchor $S$.
principalClaims.note: FULL original statement for actual mathlib integral Hadamard matrices and the standard real span of injectively selected r<n rows. Derives outside row, rational expansion and unit norm, exact least common denominator>1 dividing odd m, an actual invertible column anchor, divisibility by every normalized anchor determinant and sharp least-prime r^(r/2)/2^(r-1) bound. Seventeen original Apache2 modules54theorems and5concrete definitions; independent mathlib-only Challenge, std3audits and private both kernels. All30current public comparison groups still required; no public acceptance implied by integration.

principalClaims.title: A prime-factor lower bound for positive trade volume
principalClaims.statementTeX:
Every nonempty reduced observation trade of volume $r<n$ from such an
array satisfies \eqref{trd:bound}. In particular, if
\[
 p>\max_{1\le k\le R}\frac{k^{k/2}}{2^{k-1}},
\]
then every array in this saturated fiber is isolated under all positive
moment-preserving moves of degree at most $R$.
principalClaims.note: FULL reduced observation trade volume and bounded-degree isolation statement. Concrete normalized sign-coordinate trade preserves degree-one/two moments, and deleted/inserted disjointness only. Derives the new actual Hadamard matrix and deleted-row span, proves sharp least-prime volume bound, and derives R<n from determinant threshold rather than assuming it. principalClaims.title: A quantitative infinite subsequence
principalClaims.statementTeX:
\label{trd:linnik}
There is an infinite sequence of known Hadamard orders $n\to\infty$

\]
Equivalently, for every $\varepsilon>0$, this lower bound holds with

principalClaims.title: Residue-sensitive collision bound and equality
principalClaims.statementTeX:
\label{thm:residue-bound}
For every such law,
\[
 C(w)\le\frac1N,\qquad
 H_2(w):=-\log C(w)\ge\log N,\qquad H(w)\ge\log N.
\]
If $C(w)=1/N$, the law is uniform on exactly $N$ atoms and their
augmented sign matrix admits completion by $N-n\le3$ columns to a
Hadamard matrix of order $N$. Conversely any order-$N$ Hadamard matrix
gives a law attaining both entropy bounds. Consequently attainment
of either entropy lower bound is equivalent to Hadamard existence
at order $N$.
principalClaims.note: All three sharp inequalities are proved for actual Boolean-cube laws. Uniformity at equality and exact support cardinality are proved in all four residue classes. Actual Hadamard reconstruction retains every atom coordinate. The converse constructs an actual Boolean-cube law with both entropy values attained. Attainment of either bound is equivalent to Hadamard existence, using locally proved completion through codimension three and no conjectural existence assumption.

principalClaims.title: A positive entropy window suffices
principalClaims.statementTeX:
\label{cor:entropy-window}
For even $n\ge4$, define
\[
 \varepsilon_n=-\log\left(1-\frac4{(n-1)(n^2-4)}\right)>0.
\]
If $H(\mu)<\log n+\varepsilon_n$, the support of $\mu$ contains
$n$ mutually orthogonal augmented sign vectors. In particular it
contains an order-$n$ Hadamard matrix. Here
$\varepsilon_n\sim4/n^3$.
principalClaims.note: Complete Shannon-entropy window: unconditional positivity for every real n>=4; Shannon dominates collision entropy, and the strict window yields an actual support-selected mathlib Hadamard matrix for every isotropic even-order sign frame. Proves epsilon_n/(4/n^3) tends to1 on natural orders using the logarithm derivative at zero and the exact rational-factor limit. No asymptotic or extraction assumption.

principalClaims.title: One saturated atom in every even dimension
principalClaims.statementTeX:
\label{prop:minentropy-counter}
For every even $n\ge4$ there is a balanced pairwise-independent measure
on $n-1$ bits with $H_{\min}=\log n$. At $n=6$ this holds although
no Hadamard matrix of order $6$ exists.
principalClaims.note: Original permutation-average construction supplies an actual nonnegative Boolean-cube law in every even dimension, exact mass and first/pair moments, a saturated positive atom, and min-entropy defined as minus log of the actual largest atom. The seed is explicitly constructed in every dimension; the general atom cap proves that atom is largest. no_real_hadamard_order_six converts a hypothetical real Hadamard matrix to its integer signs and applies mathlib standard four-divisibility obstruction, proving the stated order-six counterexample.

principalClaims.title: Completion-assisted rounding
principalClaims.statementTeX:
\label{cor:completion-rounding}
Let $4\mid n$, $n\ge12$, and let $w$ be any probability measure on
$n-1$ sign bits, with $C$ and moment defect $E$ as in
Theorem~\ref{thm:discrete-rounding}. If
\[
 (n^2-4)C>n+E-\frac4{n-8},
\]
then a Hadamard matrix of order $n$ exists. If $E=0$, it suffices that
\[
 C>\frac1n-\frac{32}{n(n-8)(n^2-4)}.
\]
Equivalently a sufficient Shannon-entropy window is
\[
 H(w)<\log n-\log\left(1-\frac{32}{(n-8)(n^2-4)}\right).
\]
The entropy conclusion here assumes $E=0$.
principalClaims.note: Full source proof included; no complete Lean proof claimed.
principalClaims.formalizationScopeNote: A checked private proof exists, but source integration and public-project verification are unfinished. It is not included in the submitted formalization.

Every factor is explicitly a normalized pure complex maximally entangled state and has a zero entry, hence is nonflat. The SAME displayed ensemble defines actual complex matrices at all tensor levels, with standard positive-semidefinite predicate, trace one, permutation invariance and exact partial-trace consistency. principalClaims.title: Where the hierarchy becomes equivalent to existence
principalClaims.statementTeX:
A real Hadamard matrix of order $n$ exists if and only if there is
an infinitely exchangeable hierarchy satisfying
\begin{align*}
 \tr(\rho_2S)&=1,& \tr(\rho_2S_A)&=1/n,\\
 \tr(\rho_2(L_{ab}\otimes L_{ab}))&=0\quad(a<b),&
 \tr(\rho_2 C)&=1/n^2.
\end{align*}
Every de Finetti representing measure of such a hierarchy is supported
on vectorized real scaled Hadamard matrices, up to irrelevant phases.
principalClaims.note: Full source proof included; no complete Lean proof claimed.
principalClaims.formalizationScopeNote: The complete principal statement has not been formalized. Supporting lemmas or computational certificates do not establish the whole claim.

principalClaims.title: Rigidity of positive diagonal balancing
principalClaims.statementTeX:
Let $U\in O(n)$ and let $D,E$ be positive diagonal matrices.
If $DUE\in O(n)$, then $DUE=U$ entry by entry.
If the bipartite support graph of $U$ is connected, necessarily
$D=cI_n$ and $E=c^{-1}I_n$ for some $c>0$.
principalClaims.note: Complete entrywise rigidity for actual two-sided real orthogonality under arbitrary strictly positive row and column scalings. A nonnegative logarithmic sum proves uniqueness of doubly stochastic scaling on its support. Exact bipartite support paths then force reciprocal constant scalings. Covers empty index types too; no uniqueness or connectivity conclusion is assumed.

principalClaims.title: The natural classical and operator capacities are blind
principalClaims.statementTeX:
Let $B$ be any doubly stochastic matrix. Define
\[
 p_B(x)=\prod_{i=1}^n\left(\sum_j B_{ij}x_j\right),\qquad
 \operatorname{cap}(p_B)=\inf_{x_j>0}\frac{p_B(x)}{\prod_jx_j}.
\]
Also define the completely positive map
\[
 T_B(X)=\operatorname{diag}\bigl(B\operatorname{diag}(X)\bigr),
 \qquad
 \operatorname{cap}(T_B)=\inf_{X\succ0}
       \frac{\det T_B(X)}{\det X}.
\]
Then both capacities equal $1$. Moreover
$T_B(I)=T_B^*(I)=I$. Thus every orthogonal $U$, flat or not,
already passes these balancing and capacity tests for $B=U\circ U$.
principalClaims.note: Complete actual classical and complex operator infimum capacities equal one for every finite doubly stochastic matrix. Original weighted AM-GM product proof, unitary-square stochasticity, complex spectral diagonal and positive-definite determinant bound, exact infimum attainment at identity, explicit Kraus decomposition with all finite tensor-level positivity, Hilbert-Schmidt adjoint identity, both unital identities, and specialization to every real orthogonal matrix. No capacity, spectral-factor, adjoint or positivity assumption beyond stated hypotheses; only mathlib and original proof code with standard axioms.

principalClaims.title: Elementary parity gap
principalClaims.statementTeX:
Let $n\equiv2\pmod4$ and $U\in O(n)$. Then
\[
 F_4(U)-1\ge
 \frac{\left(\sqrt{1+\sqrt{2(n-2)/n}}-1\right)^2}{n}
 \ge \frac{2(n-2)}{9n^2}.
\]
Equivalently this lower bounds
$\|U\circ U-J_n/n\|_F^2$, since that squared distance is $F_4(U)-1$.
No optimality of the constants is asserted.
principalClaims.note: Complete all-order parity gap for every actual real orthogonal matrix at n%4=2. Proves exact integer Gram-error floor2n(n-2), casts/scales it into Frobenius norm, derives orthogonal invariance and2d+d^2 perturbation bound, original nearest-sign rounding and exact quartic variance, nested square-root lower bound and rational2(n-2)/(9n^2) bound, including n=2 endpoint. The displayed Frobenius squared-distance identity is included in the main statement. No spectral-gap or rounding hypothesis, only standard axioms.

principalClaims.title: Collision--moment rounding certificate
principalClaims.statementTeX:
\label{thm:discrete-rounding}
If
\begin{equation}\label{eq:discrete-certificate}
 (n^2-4)C>n+E-\frac4{n-1},
\end{equation}
then the support of $w$ contains $n$ atoms whose augmented vectors are
mutually orthogonal. These vectors give a Hadamard matrix of order $n$.
They can be extracted by repeated weight merging, without adding atoms.
More generally, suppose every distinct nonorthogonal pair in the support
has $|v_x\cdot v_y|\ge a$, where $0<a<n$. Then the sufficient condition is
\[
 (n^2-a^2)C>n+E-\frac{a^2}{n-1}.
\]
If the support lies in a single parity class and $4\mid n$, one may
use $a=4$ (for $n>4$), improving the constant from $4$ to $16$.
principalClaims.note: Full original finite Motzkin-Straus merging proof: mass and nonnegativity preserved, support strictly decreases, weighted edge objective does not decrease, and an explicit ReflTransGen merge chain reaches a clique. Exact actual moment-matrix/Frobenius-error identity, general nonorthogonality-gap certificate, ordinary even-order gap2 and same-parity gap4 all proved. Extracts an actual mathlib Hadamard matrix with an injective row map into the original support; no extraction assumption or additional atoms.

principalClaims.title: Explicit collision gap
principalClaims.statementTeX:
\label{cor:discrete-gap}
An exactly balanced pairwise independent measure on $n-1$ bits with
\[
 C>\frac1n-\frac4{n(n-1)(n^2-4)}
\]
contains an order-$n$ Hadamard matrix in its support. Consequently,
if no such matrix exists, every such measure satisfies the opposite
nonstrict inequality. With single-parity support, replace both occurrences
of $4$ in the correction by $16$, for $n>4$.
principalClaims.note: Exact isotropic sign-frame collision thresholds with correction4 and single-parity correction16, retaining every selected support row. Both strict-threshold extraction and unconditional nonstrict bounds under nonexistence are proved. Threshold algebra and the moment-error-zero implication are proved, using the full finite merging certificate.

principalClaims.title: Nonsingular modular seeds need not lift
principalClaims.statementTeX:
\label{prop:discrete-modular}
Let $m\ge3$, $n>4$, and $n\equiv4\pmod m$, and put $B=J_n-2I_n$.
Then $BB^T\equiv nI_n\pmod m$, but $B$ is not a real Hadamard matrix.
Moreover there is no real Hadamard matrix entrywise congruent to $B$
modulo $m$. For every odd prime $p$, the choices $n=4+4pt$ with $t\ge1$
give infinitely many admissible orders with an invertible modular seed
that has no such sign lift.
principalClaims.note: The original universal-ring calculation gives the exact Gram of J-2I, actual modular scaled orthogonality, failure of real Hadamard orthogonality, and impossibility of any entrywise congruent sign lift for every modulus at least three. infinitely_many_modular_seeds_without_lifts proves a genuinely infinite set of admissible orders for each odd prime, using the explicit invertible family n=4+4pt and matrix inverse one-quarter times the seed. No finite numerical search or assumed invertibility.

principalClaims.title: Sharp weighted collision bound
principalClaims.statementTeX:
\label{prop:discrete-parity-collision}
Let $n\ge6$ with $n\equiv2\pmod4$. Every balanced pairwise independent
measure on $n-1$ bits satisfies
\[
 C\le\frac1{n+2}.
\]
Whenever an order-$(n+2)$ Hadamard matrix exists, this bound is attained.
In particular $C\le1/8$ for five bits is sharp, whereas the general
atom estimate alone gives only $C\le1/6$.
principalClaims.note: The exact Boolean-cube collision bound in augmented dimension two modulo four is combined with actual attainment from every adjacent-order mathlib Hadamard input. five_bit_collision_eighth_attained constructs the sharp five-bit witness from the original order-eight Walsh Hadamard matrix, without an existence assumption. Original residue kernel, normalization, actual cube pushforward and Walsh proofs supply all inputs.

principalClaims.title: Equality rigidity and two-column reconstruction
principalClaims.statementTeX:
\label{thm:discrete-parity-equality}
For $n\ge6$, $n\equiv2\pmod4$, a balanced pairwise independent measure
on $n-1$ bits attains $C=1/(n+2)$ if and only if it is uniform on
$n+2$ distinct atoms whose augmented matrix can be completed by two
sign columns to an order-$(n+2)$ Hadamard matrix.
In particular the collision bound is attained if and only if an
order-$(n+2)$ Hadamard matrix exists.
principalClaims.note: Full iff for each actual Boolean-cube law: collision equality precisely characterizes uniform support of the required cardinality, together with an actual adjacent-order mathlib Hadamard matrix retaining every augmented coordinate through column and row identifications. The separate parity_collision_attainment_iff_hadamard proves both directions of the existence criterion. Original codimension-two completion and uniformity proofs are used, without an assumed classical completion theorem.

principalClaims.title: Nonnegative defect decomposition
principalClaims.note: Full exact defect identity, nonnegativity of both terms and deficit, exceptional ordered-pair mass bound with constant32, and weighted distance-to-uniform bound are proved for actual integer sign frames under the stated coordinate isotropy. No extraction assumption is used.

principalClaims.title: Explicit extraction from a sufficiently small deficit
principalClaims.statementTeX:
If $\delta\le1/(1024N^4)$, the set
\[
 G=\{x:|Nw_x-1|\le1/(4N)\}
\]
has exactly $N$ members. Giving those members equal weight $1/N$
preserves exact isotropy. Their augmented sign rows can consequently
be completed by three sign columns to a Hadamard matrix of order $N$.
Thus, if no Hadamard matrix of order $N$ exists, every such isotropic
distribution has $C<1/N-1/(1024N^4)$.
principalClaims.note: Full explicit threshold1/(1024N^4) extraction is proved: exactlyN good atoms, exact uniformized coordinate isotropy by integer quantization, actual Hadamard reconstruction retaining every selected atom coordinate, and the strict nonexistence collision gap.

principalClaims.title: Collision cost of full coordinate symmetry
principalClaims.statementTeX:
\label{thm:symmetry-collision}
For $d\ge7$,
\[
 C(w)\le B_d:=\frac1{d^2}+\frac d{(d-2)^4}
                    +\frac2{d(d-1)}<\frac4{d^2}.
\]
The maximal collision probability among such symmetric laws is
$\Theta(d^{-2})$. For every $d\ge5$, no such law attains the
residue-sensitive optimum
$1/N$, $N=4\lceil(d+1)/4\rceil$.
For each $d\in\{2,3,4\}$ a symmetric law attaining that bound exists.
principalClaims.note: FULL collision symmetry theorem: actual B_d upper envelope and strict 4/d^2 bound; compactness gives an actual maximizing law; canonical supremum has formal Asymptotics.IsTheta inverse-square rate, supported by explicit matching odd/even slice laws. Equality rigidity and exact orbit counts prove nonattainment in dimensions5,6, combined with strict bounds for all d>=7. Explicit pairwise-independent probability laws attain the residue-sensitive optimum at dimensions2,3,4. All probability, symmetry, orbit, moment, binomial, endpoint and collision formulas are proved. Seven strict mathlib-only targets, zero definition holes, fifteen source-bound module receipts, original Apache-2.0 proofs and standard three axioms; private both-kernel acceptance. Fresh integrated fourteen-group verification required.

principalClaims.title: Shannon entropy is almost maximal
principalClaims.statementTeX:
\label{thm:symmetry-shannon}
Every such symmetric pairwise-independent law satisfies
\[
 H(w)\ge(d-1)\log2-\log(d+1).
\]
Thus full coordinate symmetry forces Shannon entropy to within
$O(\log d)$ of the maximum $d\log2$, rather than the desired
order $\log d$.
principalClaims.note: Full Shannon entropy lower bound for actual coordinate-permutation-invariant unbiased pairwise-independent laws on d>=2 Boolean coordinates. Original proofs: coordinate orbit classification and exact slice cardinality; atom caps imply slice entropy lower bound; binomial recurrence and mode yield log binomial >= d h(k/d)-log(d+1); integral harmonic inequality proves h(p)>=4log(2)p(1-p); actual Hamming moments complete the bound. No unproved entropy, mode, orbit or approximation assumptions. One mathlib-only strict target with zero definition holes. Original Apache-2.0 proofs, standard three axioms, private both-kernel acceptance and six raw source/olean receipts. Fresh integrated thirteen-group verification required.

principalClaims.title: Local maximum criterion
principalClaims.statementTeX:
\label{lem:attainment-criterion}
A point $w$ of a finite polytope $P$ is a local maximum of the squared
Euclidean norm if and only if $w$ uniquely maximizes the linear
functional $v\mapsto w\cdot v$ over $P$. In this case it is a strict
local maximum and a vertex. In particular, every uniform distribution
that is a vertex of $\mathcal P_d$ is a strict local maximum of $C$.
principalClaims.note: Full finite-polytope iff between local squared-norm maximality and unique maximization of the own inner-product functional, with strict-local and actual mathlib extreme-point conclusions. Separately proves every uniform vertex of an arbitrary finite probability affine-moment polytope is a strict local collision maximum, using a proved compact tangent-cone margin, not a finite-vertex representation assumption. Explicitly proves the Boolean-cube probability/mean/pair constraints equal the matrix moment model and specializes the theorem to the actual full cube polytope.

principalClaims.title: Explicit four- and five-bit traps
principalClaims.note: Full exact four- and five-bit laws with the paper weight-by-negative-count formulas, actual cube probability/mean/pair constraints, collision7/72, strict local maxima on the full feasible polytope and explicit feasible witnesses of larger collision1/8. principalClaims.title: A trap at admissible Hadamard order eight
principalClaims.statementTeX:
\label{thm:attainment-admissible-trap}
Let $z$ be uniform on $\mathbb F_2^4$, and take seven sign bits
$x_b(z)=(-1)^{b\cdot z}$ with
\[
 B=\{1,2,3,4,5,8,10\},
\]

Unit-bounded Walsh interpolation is constructed and proved. Finite arithmetic certificates use kernel reduction, not native evaluation.

principalClaims.title: Arbitrarily poor traps at admissible orders
principalClaims.statementTeX:
\label{thm:attainment-infinite-traps}
For every integer $s\ge2$, put $h=2^s$. There is a uniform vertex
of $\mathcal P_{2h-1}$ supported on $h^2$ atoms. It is a strict
local maximum with collision $1/h^2$, whereas the global maximum
is $1/(2h)$. Their ratio $2/h$ tends to zero. A sufficient strict
local radius in the infinity norm is $2/[h^2(h^2+1)]$.
principalClaims.note: Full actual two-seed cube-law family at every s>=2: proves observation dimension2h-1 and admissible order, feasible uniform law on h^2 distinct atoms, actual mathlib extreme-point membership, strict local collision maximum with explicit infinity radius2/(h^2(h^2+1)), collision1/h^2, attained global maximum1/(2h), and ratio2/h tending tozero. Constructs actual unit-bounded Walsh interpolation functions with delta support values and fixed moment expectations. principalClaims.title: A certified collision barrier
principalClaims.statementTeX:
\label{cor:attainment-barrier}
For each uniform character trap above with support size $m$, every
continuous feasible path from the trap to a global maximizer passes
through a measure of collision at most
\[
 \frac1m-\frac1{m^2(m+1)}.
\]
principalClaims.note: Full continuous-path barrier for both preceding uniform character examples: every feasible continuous path from the actual infinite two-seed trap or the exact order-eight mask trap to a global maximizer crosses collision<=1/m-1/(m^2(m+1)). The proof establishes the unit-bounded interpolation estimates, exact shell deficit and intermediate-value crossing; global endpoint values1/(2h) and1/8 are explicit and their strict improvement is proved.

principalClaims.title: Complete rigidity from additive coverage
principalClaims.statementTeX:
\label{thm:character-cover}
The observed bits are unbiased and pairwise independent if and only if
\[
 \widehat p(c)=0\quad\text{for every }c\in(A+A)\setminus\{0\}.
\]
Consequently, if $A+A=G$, the only feasible seed law is uniform.
In particular this holds whenever $|A|>L/2$.
If $c\notin A+A$, the family
\[
 p_t(z)=\frac{1+t\chi_c(z)}L,\qquad -1\le t\le1,
\]
is feasible and has collision $(1+t^2)/L$. At $t=\pm1$ it is uniform
on an affine hyperplane of size $L/2$ and doubles the collision.
Thus missing additive directions give explicit compression steps,
whereas full coverage forbids every seed-reweighting step.
principalClaims.note: Actual Walsh characters satisfy the moment/coverage equivalence. Full coverage forces uniformity, and more than half the masks covers. Every missing direction gives nonnegative normalized laws with all required moments and exact collision (1+t^2)/2^r. The endpoint laws are uniform on exactly half the seeds. An explicit bijective binary coordinate map identifies their supports with fibers of a nonzero linear functional over ZMod 2, with kernel dimension r-1. Spanning observables are injective and preserve collision under pushforward.

principalClaims.title: The smallest binary seed forces a power-of-two law
principalClaims.statementTeX:
\label{cor:minimum-seed}
If $r=\lceil\log_2(d+1)\rceil$, any feasible law with these linear
observables is uniform on $L=2^r$ distinct atoms, even when arbitrary
seed weights are allowed.
For a non-power-of-two multiple of four $N\ge12$, take $d=N-4$.
Then this construction class has collision deficit
\[
 \frac1N-C=\frac1N-\frac1L>\frac2{N^2},
\]
far larger than the sufficient extraction window $1/(1024N^4)$.
principalClaims.note: The least binary seed size is expressed by the natural ceiling logarithm Nat.clog. The actual observed law has uniform nonzero weights, exactly 2^r distinct atoms, and collision 1/2^r. For every non-power-of-two multiple of four N>=12, its deficit is strictly greater than 2/N^2 and the stated extraction threshold.

principalClaims.title: Approximate moment version
principalClaims.statementTeX:
\label{prop:approx-character}
Suppose $A+A=G$ and every observed mean and pair correlation has
absolute value at most $\varepsilon$. Then
\[
 C(p)=\frac1L\left(1+\sum_{c\ne0}\widehat p(c)^2\right)
 \le\frac1L+\frac{L-1}{L}\varepsilon^2.
\]
In particular, if $C(p)\ge1/N-\eta$ with $N<L$, necessarily
\[
 \varepsilon^2\ge
 \frac{L/N-1-L\eta}{L-1}
\]
whenever the right side is positive.
principalClaims.note: Full finite Walsh inversion and Parseval are proved from character orthogonality. Additive coverage converts every nonconstant coefficient into an observed mean or pair correlation, giving the exact collision expansion, its epsilon-square upper bound, and the lower bound on epsilon^2 for near-target collision.

principalClaims.title: Maximum overlap and optimal straight bridge
principalClaims.statementTeX:
\label{thm:compression-optimal-overlap}
Every pairwise-orthogonal subset of augmented trap rows has size at most
$h$, and $h$ is attained. Consequently every global collision maximizer
on $2h-1$ unbiased pairwise-independent bits has at most $h$ atoms in
common with the trap. The endpoint \eqref{eq:compression-endpoint}
attains this maximum overlap. Along the feasible affine bridge
$\mu_\lambda=(1-\lambda)\mu+\lambda\nu$,
\[
 C(\mu_\lambda)=\frac{1-\lambda+(h/2)\lambda^2}{h^2},\qquad
 \min_{0\le\lambda\le1}C(\mu_\lambda)
 =\frac{1-1/(2h)}{h^2},
\]
with the minimum at $\lambda=1/h$.
Among all straight mixture bridges from this trap to a global maximizer,
this minimum is as large as possible. The optimal collision loss is
exactly $1/(2h^3)$.
principalClaims.note: The exact augmented trap Gram formula, orthogonality criterion, injective row encoding, sharp maximum orthogonal-subset size, and permutation graph with constant mixed sign are proved. Both actual probability laws on 2h-1 observed bits are feasible and have exact uniform supports, collisions and h shared atoms. The endpoint is a global maximizer. Every global maximizer has at most h shared trap atoms and a pointwise no-better straight bridge. The constructed feasible bridge has the stated polynomial, attained minimum at 1/h, and exact loss 1/(2h^3). No optimality over curved paths is claimed.

principalClaims.title: Complete any maximum overlap subset
principalClaims.note: For every actual orthogonal h-element subset of augmented trap row vectors, an explicit two-block Walsh construction yields a standard mathlib Hadamard matrix of order 2h, retaining every chosen row through an injection. principalClaims.title: Finite nonlocal rewiring
principalClaims.statementTeX:
\label{prop:compression-jumps}
The $h-1$ jumps just described preserve unbiased pairwise independence

Rank preservation keeps support and collision, and a one-rank drop halves support and doubles collision. The actual masks remain injective and observed characters nonzero. The initial swap, one-column updates, h-1-jump schedule, feasibility of every endpoint, and exact final endpoint law are proved. The Boolean laws are identified with the binary linear laws, actual updates factor as rank-one repairs, endpoint collision never decreases, and exactly s-1 jumps halve support and double collision while h-s preserve both. The joined affine segments are feasible, start at the trap law, end at the compressed law, and have exact attained minimum 3/(4h^2).

principalClaims.title: Nonnegative exact correction
principalClaims.note: Actual Boolean-cube Walsh characters, coefficient polynomial and maximal buffer are defined explicitly. Finite orthogonality is proved from coordinate-flip involutions. All normalization, positivity, first/pair moment, variation and exact collision conclusions are proved.

principalClaims.title: A sufficient input window for exact extraction
principalClaims.statementTeX:
Let $d=n-1$, $n\equiv1\pmod4$, $n\ge5$, and $N=n+3$.
If $C(P)\ge1/N$ and $B\le1/(2048N^3)$, the corrected law satisfies
\[

\]
Consequently the quantitative residue-one extraction theorem of round6

It suffices to replace the assumption on $B$ by the stronger,
easier-to-check condition $L\le1/(2048N^3)$.

principalClaims.title: Quantization obstruction for a uniform row candidate
principalClaims.statementTeX:

\[
 1/N-C(Q)\ge1/(2N^2),
\]

principalClaims.title: Affine observable budget
principalClaims.statementTeX:
\label{prop:nonlinear-affine-budget}
Suppose an order-$N$ normalized Hadamard matrix is encoded by distinct
labels $S\subset\mathbb F_2^r$, with uniform weight $1/N$ on each label.
If $N\equiv4\pmod8$ and $r<N-2$, the number $k$ of nonconstant columns
that extend to affine Boolean functions satisfies
\[
 k\le\min\{r,\,2^r-N-1\}\qquad(N<2^r).
\]
Thus a minimal four-bit encoding of $H_{12}$ needs at least eight
nonaffine observables, and a minimal five-bit encoding of $H_{20}$
needs at least fourteen.
principalClaims.note: Full affine-observable budget for actual normalized integer Hadamard matrices and every injective r-bit encoding, with exactly the stated N mod8=4,r<N-2,N<2^r hypotheses: intrinsic affine-extension count k<=min(r,2^r-N-1). Counts every possible affine function agreeing on seed labels, not merely a chosen extension. Matrix-to-Boolean strength-two link, any proper selected-column augmented binary independence, affine code dimension and complementary Walsh-character dimension all proved. Numeric12/20corollaries give at least8/14nonaffine columns. Exact code1dimension r+1 and general affine support indicator residue obstruction also independently targeted. principalClaims.title: Complement criterion for low-degree extensions
principalClaims.statementTeX:
\label{lem:nonlinear-extension}
Every Boolean function on $S\subset\mathbb F_2^r$ has a degree-at-most-$d$
extension if and only if there is no nonzero polynomial of degree at
most $r-d-1$ supported entirely on $S$. In particular, cubic extensions
exist on any proper subset of the four-bit cube. On five bits they
exist whenever the complement of $S$ affinely spans the cube.
principalClaims.note: Complete concrete Reed-Muller restriction criterion, including four-bit cubic extension on every proper support and five-bit cubic extension when the actual complement affinely spans. Original squarefree monomial independence, dimension, full-cube duality, zero-extension and finite nondegenerate restriction proof. Supporting declarations four_bit_cubic_extension and five_bit_affine_complement_cubic_extension independently targeted. Standard three axioms, zero definition holes. principalClaims.title: Sharp cubic benchmarks at orders twelve and twenty
principalClaims.statementTeX:
\label{thm:nonlinear-cubic}
For $N=12$ and $N=20$, the least possible maximum Boolean degree of
all $N-1$ observables, among encodings on the minimal number
$r=\lceil\log_2N\rceil$ of binary seed bits, is exactly three.
The affine budgets above are simultaneously sharp: the examples have

principalClaims.note: Complete sharp cubic benchmarks. Universal lower bounds quantify over every actual normalized integer Hadamard matrix and every injective minimal-bit full-column encoding, ruling out all-quadratic outputs at orders12 and20. Original explicit H12/H20 matrices satisfy standard mathlib Matrix.IsHadamard; all cubic polynomials and truth matches kernel-certified. Private both kernels passed; integrated seven-group verification required.

principalClaims.title: Fixed algebraic degree cannot suffice asymptotically
principalClaims.statementTeX:
\label{cor:nonlinear-growing-degree}
For any Hadamard order $N\ge12$ with $N\equiv4\pmod8$, and minimal
binary seed length $r=\lceil\log_2N\rceil$, every encoding has maximum
Boolean degree at least $\lceil r/2\rceil$. Conversely, every injection
of its rows into the $r$-bit cube admits extensions of degree at most
$r-1$. Thus a fixed-degree minimal-seed model cannot represent extremal
laws in arbitrarily large such orders, even where Hadamard matrices
are already known.
principalClaims.note: Complete lower and upper degree bounds for minimal injective binary seed encodings at N>=12,N mod8=4. Stronger lower bound already follows from N-2 actual unbiased pairwise-independent outputs; concrete binary Gram and augmented-column independence proved, not assumed. Minimum seed length is expressed by 2^(r-1)<N<=2^r, and lower bound r<=2*d is equivalent to d>=ceil(r/2). Every truth function on every injective labeling extends with degree at most r-1. Standard three axioms, original Apache-2.0 code, independent fully concrete zero-definition-hole Challenge. Private both kernels passed; integrated verification required.

principalClaims.title: Actual positive correction with an explicit margin
principalClaims.statementTeX:
Suppose $A$ has full row rank, and define
\[
 R=A^T(AA^T)^{-1},\quad
 \gamma=\max_j\sum_a|R_{ja}|,\quad
 m=Ap-b,\quad \tau=\|m\|_\infty.
\]
For any probability vector $p$ with $p_{\min}\ge\gamma\tau$, the
vector $q=p-Rm$ is a nonnegative probability vector on the same
support and satisfies $Aq=b$. In particular this is an exact
distribution correction, not an unconstrained projection being
mistaken for a probability law. It obeys
\[
 \|q-p\|_\infty\le\gamma\tau,\quad
 d_{\rm TV}(p,q)\le s\gamma\tau/2,\quad
 C(q)\ge C(p)-2\gamma\tau.
\]
principalClaims.note: The actual Gram inverse right inverse is derived from full row rank. Its maximum absolute row sum gives positivity, exact normalization and constraints, coordinate distance, total variation, and collision lower bounds. The theorem accepts any nonnegative upper bound on all residual coordinates, including their infinity norm. The stated small-error extraction criterion is also proved, with actual sign moments encoded among the constraint rows.

principalClaims.title: No adaptive reweighting on a minimal-size support
principalClaims.statementTeX:
Let $N\ge8$ be divisible by four, $d=N-4$, and $S$ have at most $N$
distinct sign vectors. If an unbiased pairwise-independent law exists
on $S$, its positive support has exactly $N$ members and its weights
are all $1/N$. Its augmented sign rows complete to a Hadamard matrix
of order $N$.
Consequently, if the uniform law on a given $N$-point set is not
isotropic, no reweighting on that same set can make it isotropic.
principalClaims.note: Actual finite sign frames supported on at most the sharp rounded dimension have exactly that many atoms, all uniform positive weights, and a genuine Hadamard completion. Failed uniform frames admit no probability reweighting on the same support. The statement is proved in all residue classes, strengthening the stated residue-one case.

principalClaims.title: Binary rank of a minimal-support target
principalClaims.statementTeX:
\label{lem:rank-target}
For such a target, let $Y$ be the $N\times d$ binary matrix with
$Y_{ij}=(1-x_{ij})/2$. Then
\[
 Y^TY=I_d+J_d\quad\text{over }\mathbb F_2,
 \qquad \operatorname{rank}_{\mathbb F_2}Y=d.
\]
principalClaims.note: For actual N-row binary strength-two arrays with N>=12 and N=4 mod8, the original proof constructs the bit matrix over ZMod 2, derives the exact Gram I+J from its pair counts and column parity, explicitly squares I+J to the identity, and proves actual mathlib matrix rank N-4. The target assumes neither a binary Gram nor a rank certificate. It applies to every uniform minimal-support target through the proved equality/array correspondence.

principalClaims.title: Support-overlap rigidity
principalClaims.statementTeX:
\label{thm:rank-overlap}
If a binary linear code $\mathcal C\subseteq\mathbb F_2^d$ has
dimension at most $r$, every minimal-support target intersects it in
at most $r+4$ atoms. Consequently a uniform $N$-point candidate
supported in $\mathcal C$ has total-variation distance at least
\[
 1-\frac{r+4}{N}
\]
from every exactly pairwise-independent law on at most $N$ points.
At least $N-r-4$ atoms must be replaced; changing their weights alone
cannot avoid this conclusion.
principalClaims.note: The complete theorem handles every nonnegative exact Boolean-cube law on at most N atoms, deriving uniformity and exact support size from the proved minimal-support theorem. It reconstructs the actual strength-two target array, derives its binary rank, bounds intersection with any uniform N-point candidate in a binary code of dimension at most r by r+4, proves the actual half-L1 total-variation lower bound, and proves at least N-r-4 new target atoms are required. No uniformity, rank, Gram, or overlap certificate is assumed. Thus reweighting alone is covered by the same unconditional bound.

principalClaims.title: An explicit near-moment candidate
principalClaims.statementTeX:
\label{prop:rank-walsh-candidate}
Let $L=2^r$, $d=N-4\ge L/2$, and $N\le L$. Observe the distinct
characters with binary masks $1,\ldots,d$ on $\mathbb F_2^r$.
Choose any $N$ seed points and give them equal weights. The resulting
law $P$ has $N$ distinct atoms,
\[
 C(P)=1/N,\qquad
 \max_{1\le|S|\le2}|\mathbb E_P\chi_S|\le\frac{L-N}{N}.
\]
Nevertheless its distance from every minimal-support target is at
least $1-(r+4)/N$.
It is simultaneously close to an exactly feasible law: if $U$ is
the full uniform Walsh law, then
\[
 d_{\rm TV}(P,U)=1-N/L,\qquad C(U)=1/L.
\]
principalClaims.note: Full finite candidate theorem for the actual initial binary masks 1 through d, any N selected seed points, and the constructed pushforward laws. It proves injectivity and N distinct output atoms, normalization and positivity, exact collision 1/N, every first/pair error bound, exact distance 1-N/L to the full Walsh law, exact full-law pairwise independence and collision 1/L, and separation from every nonnegative exact law on at most N atoms. The binary encoder and dimension bound are proved, not supplied as assumptions.

principalClaims.title: A nonvacuous asymptotic obstruction to dimension-free rounding
principalClaims.note: Full original proof constructs actual unbounded Paley orders and laws, uniform moment error tending to zero, nearby exact laws with relative collision tending to one, nonempty minimal-support exact classes, and universal total-variation separation tending to one. No distribution hypothesis.

principalClaims.title: Even restriction code and its radical
principalClaims.statementTeX:
\label{lem:nonlinear-radical}
Let $C=\mathrm{RM}(r-2,r)|_S$ be the binary restriction code, with
$C_0$ its even-weight subcode. Then
\[
 \dim C=N-a,\quad \dim C_0=N-a-1,\quad
 \dim\operatorname{rad}(C_0)=a+1,
\]
where the radical uses the binary dot product. Consequently its bilinear
rank is $N-2a-2$.
principalClaims.note: All four exact identities for arbitrary proper cube supports of size 4 mod8, r>=4: restriction dimension N-a, even-code dimension N-a-1, actual binary-dot-product radical dimension a+1, and bilinear row-space rank N-2a-2. The parameter a is r minus the dimension of the vector span of the omitted points, exactly their affine codimension for a nonempty complement. Affine-vanishing/annihilator and restriction-dual equivalences are proved. Canonical row-space rank avoids generated instance-proof alias instability. Original Apache-2.0 code; strict independent target, no definition holes; private both kernels and standard three-axiom audit passed. Integrated nine-group verification required.

principalClaims.title: Exact fixed-support criterion for a full basis
principalClaims.statementTeX:
\label{thm:nonlinear-fixed-support}
Suppose an order-$N$ Hadamard matrix exists. The support $S$ admits
$N-1$ unbiased pairwise-independent sign observables of degree at most
$r-2$ if and only if $T$ affinely spans $\mathbb F_2^r$.
If $T$ does span, every prescribed row labeling of any such Hadamard
matrix admits observables with this degree bound.

Necessity applies already to N-2 strength-two outputs; sufficiency extends every prescribed row labeling of every given Hadamard matrix. Restriction surjectivity iff omitted labels affinely span is proved by finite-dimensional separation. A full binary array forces its restriction code to be full or even; the latter contradicts the residue-four affine-indicator weight obstruction. Three independent mathlib-only strict targets, zero definition holes, standard three axioms. Private both-kernel comparison passed; integrated nine-group verification required.

principalClaims.title: Degree saturation near a power of two
principalClaims.statementTeX:
\label{cor:nonlinear-degree-saturation}
Assume $2^{r-1}<N<2^r$, $N\equiv4\pmod8$, and $H_N$ exists.
There is some minimal-seed encoding of degree at most $r-2$ if and
only if $2^r-N\ge r+1$. If $2^r-N\le r$, the smallest possible maximum
degree is exactly $r-1$. In particular every existing
$H_{2^r-4}$, $r\ge4$, requires degree exactly $r-1$ on a minimal seed.
principalClaims.note: Complete degree-saturation result for actual normalized integer Hadamard matrices. Existence of a degree r-2 injective seed encoding iff at least r+1 cube labels are omitted, using an explicit binary affine basis and finite superset construction. Arbitrary proper labelings have degree r-1 extensions; monotonicity rules out every smaller degree when the complement has at most r points. The order 2^r-4 exact-degree specialization is separately targeted. Three strict independent mathlib-only targets, no definition holes, standard three axioms; private both kernels passed. Fresh integrated nine-group verification required.

principalClaims.title: Punctured-observable bounds, without completion
principalClaims.statementTeX:
\label{thm:nonlinear-punctured}
Let $N\equiv4\pmod8$ and let $N$ equal-weight seed labels carry $m=N-4$
unbiased pairwise-independent sign bits, all of Boolean degree at most
$d$. Then
\[
 \sum_{j=0}^d\binom rj\ge N-3.
\]
At minimal $r=\lceil\log_2N\rceil$, this forces
$d\ge\lceil r/2\rceil$. For degree at most $r-2$, the sharper necessary
condition on the omitted labels is $\operatorname{affdim}(T)\ge r-1$.
For $N=2^r-4$ and $r\ge5$, degree $r-2$ is impossible for this punctured
input, not only for a full Hadamard basis.
principalClaims.note: Complete punctured N-4 observable bounds, using actual uniform balanced pairwise-independent Boolean arrays on arbitrary proper supports in the section's r>=4,N>=12 regime. Includes the literal binomial sum >=N-3, r<=2d for minimal binary seeds, affine complement dimension >=r-1 at degree <=r-2, and the separately targeted impossibility for every support of size 2^r-4,r>=5. Real balanced and pair moments are encoded as exact integer sign sums. No completion to a full Hadamard matrix is assumed. Independent two-target mathlib-only Challenge, zero definition holes, original Apache-2.0 code, private both kernels and standard three-axiom audit passed. Integrated nine-group verification required.

principalClaims.title: Exact finite obstruction
principalClaims.statementTeX:
\label{prop:nonlinear-twelve-classification}
For a uniform law on any twelve labels in $\mathbb F_2^4$, the largest
number of unbiased pairwise-independent quadratic sign observables is:
\[
 \begin{cases}
 5,&\text{if the four omitted labels form an affine plane},\\
 7,&\text{if they are affinely independent}.
 \end{cases}
\]
In particular the order-twelve $N-4=8$-bit extraction input requires
at least one cubic observable, for every labeling.
principalClaims.note: Complete sharp5/7 classification for every twelve-label support by actual omitted affine dimension, actual degree-two code membership and uniform balanced pair moments; exact normalization/coverage, kernel-checked parity graph bounds and actual lower witnesses. Independent7theorem/7definition private dual-kernel check passed; public verification pending.

principalClaims.title: A finite exact escape rule
principalClaims.statementTeX:
At any weighted vertex $a=s/3$, choose any $i\in\{1,\ldots,5\}$
and replace the law by the uniform vertex $b=s_i e_i$.
This is an edge move of the feasible moment polytope, preserves all
normalization, positivity and pairwise constraints, and changes
twelve atom weights. It increases collision by exactly $1/36$.
Along its feasible interpolation $a(t)=(1-t)a+tb$,
\[
 C(a(t))=\frac7{72}-\frac{t}{36}+\frac{t^2}{18}.
\]
It initially decreases collision, returns to the initial value at
$t=1/2$, and reaches its minimum $3/32$ at $t=1/4$.
principalClaims.note: Full exact rule for each of sixteen weighted translates and each aligned choice among the five uniform parity coordinates. The segment is proved nondegenerate and IsExposed in the full actual probability/moment polytope. The moment-kernel restricted to the twelve-atom union is exactly the edge-direction line, with explicit minimal-support circuit conclusion and twelve changed entries. All interpolation feasibility, exact collision polynomial, improvement1/36, initial decrease, return at1/2 and minimum3/32 at1/4 are proved. Original finite rational lower-bound certificate and generic exposed-segment support-kernel proof; no external code or assumed edge/circuit oracle.

principalClaims.title: The unavoidable barrier is exactly $1/288$
principalClaims.statementTeX:
Every continuous feasible path from a weighted vertex to any uniform
vertex passes through a law of collision at most $3/32$.
The preceding edge path attains this upper bound on its minimum, so
it is optimal in the maximin sense. In particular no continuously
collision-nondecreasing path escapes a weighted vertex to an optimum.
principalClaims.note: All sixteen translated weighted laws and all ten uniform parity laws, with the full actual cube mean/pair constraints. Original finite integer Walsh kernel and rational moment certificates prove reconstruction, exact collision identity and endpoint parameters. A proved four-coordinate Hadamard square identity bounds every half-coordinate crossing, and IVT yields the unavoidable1/288 collision loss on every continuous feasible path. An explicit aligned straight path attains minimum3/32 at1/4, proving sharpness; no monotone escape exists. E22.01 remains pending its separate edge/circuit clauses. All proof code original; standard axioms only.

principalClaims.title: A quantitative moment-error floor
principalClaims.statementTeX:
\label{thm:nonlinear-moment-floor}
Suppose $m=N-4$ Boolean sign observables $X_1,\ldots,X_m$ have exact
zero means on $S$, with degree at most $r-2$. They need not be pairwise
independent. At least $\max\{0,2a-3\}$ unordered pairs have nonzero
correlation. In particular their augmented moment error satisfies
\[
 E:=\left\|\mathbb E[(1,X)(1,X)^T]-I_{m+1}\right\|_F^2
 \ge\frac{32}{N^2}\max\{0,2a-3\}.
\]
For four omitted labels and $r\ge5$, this gives
$E\ge32(2r-9)/N^2$, since $a\ge r-3$.
principalClaims.note: Complete quantitative moment-error floor for actual balanced Boolean observables of degree at most r-2 on every proper seed support with N=4 mod8,r>=4. Proves at least max(0,2a-3) unordered nonzero correlations and actual augmented Gram Frobenius error >=32 max(0,2a-3)/N^2, without pairwise independence. The explicit four-omitted-label consequence E>=32(2r-9)/N^2 is independently targeted. Divisibility of balanced integer correlations by4 is proved. Removing one endpoint per nonzero pair leaves an uncorrelated family; its actual even-code bilinear rank gives the count bound. No assumed graph rank, divisibility or completion hypothesis; no N>=12 restriction added. Two mathlib-only strict targets, zero definition holes, seven source-bound module receipts, original Apache-2.0 proofs, standard three axioms and private both-kernel acceptance. Fresh integrated eleven-group verification required.

principalClaims.title: Minimum support edits to unlock degree repair
principalClaims.statementTeX:
\label{thm:nonlinear-minimum-edits}
For this support operation no congruence condition on $N$ is needed.
Assume $|T|\ge r+1$. The smallest number of one-for-one seed support
exchanges needed to make the omitted labels affinely span the entire
$r$-space is exactly $a=r-\operatorname{affdim}(T)$.
For any already-known exact law carried on $S$, its output truth rows
can be transferred through these exchanges while preserving its entire
observable distribution, hence every moment and its collision probability.
All intermediate truth functions can have degree at most $r-1$; at the
final support they can have degree at most $r-2$.
principalClaims.note: Complete minimum support-exchange theorem: for every omitted label set T with |T|>=r+1, an actual sequence of exactly r-affdim(T) one-for-one erase/insert exchanges reaches a spanning complement, and every spanning exchange path has at least that length. No congruence condition on N. The full arbitrary output truth-row law is preserved at EVERY intermediate state by explicit coordinate transpositions; the copied row and unchanged other rows are proved. Every state admits degree r-1 Boolean-code extensions, and the final state admits degree r-2, without changing any truth value at positive-mass labels. Exact law equality implies every moment and collision is preserved. The target holds for r>=2, covering the section r>=4 context, and arbitrary output dimensions/arrays. Three strict mathlib-only targets, zero definition holes, ten source-bound module receipts, original Apache-2.0 proofs, standard three axioms and private both-kernel acceptance. principalClaims.title: An exact monotone support-reduction algorithm
principalClaims.statementTeX:
Given any rational feasible law $p$ with support $S$, repeat the
following operation while the columns $A_S$ are dependent.
Choose nonzero $z\in\ker A_S$, reverse its sign if necessary so
$p\cdot z\ge0$, and set
\[
 t=\min_{j:z_j<0}\frac{p_j}{-z_j},\qquad p\leftarrow p+tz.
\]
Every intermediate law remains nonnegative and exactly feasible,
collision increases strictly at each nontrivial step, and the entire
interpolating path has nondecreasing collision. After at most
$|S|-\operatorname{rank}A_S$ steps it reaches a vertex supported on
at most $1+d+\binom d2$ atoms. All calculations can be rational.
principalClaims.note: A finite path has at most support-cardinality minus active-matrix-rank steps, strictly increases collision at each step, and terminates at an actual extreme point with support at most the constraint count. Each step has a nonzero oriented kernel direction and the exact minimum-ratio endpoint (normalized to step size one); its entire interpolation is feasible and collision-monotone. All results hold over an arbitrary ordered field, and an explicit rational specialization keeps every matrix, direction, ratio and law rational. A separate rational-to-real proof gives an actual vertex of the real moment polytope and the step bound using the real constraint rank.

principalClaims.title: Sharp barrier for a specified straight bridge
principalClaims.statementTeX:
Let $p,q\in\mathcal P_d$ be distinct and set
$a=C(p)$, $b=C(q)\ge a$, $c=p\cdot q$, $e=a+b-2c>0$.
The feasible bridge $p_t=(1-t)p+tq$ has minimum collision
\[
 \min_{0\le t\le1}C(p_t)
 =a-\frac{(a-c)_+^2}{a+b-2c}.
\]
The minimizer is $t=(a-c)_+/e\le1/2$. Its collision loss is at most
$a^2/(a+b)\le a/2$, with the first bound attained for disjoint
supports. If $c\ge a$ the bridge is monotone and has no loss.
principalClaims.note: For actual finite probability laws, the explicit positive-part minimizer attains the exact bridge minimum, lies in [0,1/2], and has the sharp loss bounds, including disjoint-support equality. All prescribed linear moments are preserved along the bridge.

principalClaims.title: A support witness against all Hadamard mixtures
principalClaims.statementTeX:
\label{lem:design-support-witness}
If $\mu$ is any probability measure supported on $S$, then
\[
 \inf_{\nu\in\mathcal H_n}\|\mu-\nu\|_{\rm TV}

principalClaims.title: Exponential cost of full permutation symmetry
principalClaims.statementTeX:
Let $N_{\mathrm{sym}}(d)$ be the least positive run count for a binary
strength-two array whose pattern multiplicities are invariant under all

\[

For $d\ge2$,
\[
 \binom d{k_d}\ \le N_{\mathrm{sym}}(d)

\]
In particular $N_{\mathrm{sym}}(d)=\Theta(2^d/\sqrt d)$.

principalClaims.statementTeX:
\label{s33:thm:renyi-phase}
There is a unique $\alpha_*\in(6,7)$ satisfying
\[

\]

finite $\alpha>1$. Thus varying the entropy order does not force
the competing local minima to disappear at the global transition.
